No. The land-change method could not evaluate this property (ASSET-J). The analysis run on 2026-11-12 returned an error: the source coverage the asset needs has not been prepared, so no observation was made.

This means there are no results at all. The tool did not find zero land change; it never looked. You shouldn't read this as evidence that the property is clear of tree-cover loss or any other change since the 2020-12-31 baseline.

The run metadata also lists no asset area (it is null), which may be related to the missing coverage, though the output doesn't say so.

To get an assessment, the source coverage for this asset needs to be prepared and the analysis re-run. Until then, the property's land-change status is unknown.
